sent_to_model:
I'm replying to someone in an online relationship discussion whose situation reminded me a lot of something I went through. I ended up seeing a girl without putting a name on it because I still had feelings about my ex and wasn't ready for another relationship. I'd like help writing a comment about how we got together and why that arrangement suited us at first. My ex eventually got involved and things changed, including us trying to be monogamous. I want to tell them what happened and why I think that pressure helped ruin something that had been going well. We're no longer together, but I still think it could have worked if we'd been allowed to get there ourselves.

- No longer involved with the newer girl.
- Arrangement without exclusivity lasted roughly a year before the ex intervened.
- Previous serious relationship lasted four or five years; painful aftermath.
- Was open with the newer girl about unresolved feelings for the ex and uncertainty about dating again.
- Had two other encounters during the nonexclusive arrangement; last one about six months before the discussion about exclusivity.
- Spent about two years after the breakup avoiding romantic involvement, apart from a couple of one-night stands.
- Both agreed to leave their involvement undefined; neither relationship nor friends with benefits felt like the right label.
- Agreed when the newer girl requested an exclusive relationship; initially it went reasonably well.
- Ex unexpectedly reappeared and directed cruel comments at the newer girl about both her and me.
- Late conversation with the newer girl: tiredness, increasing silliness, flirting and affection, then admitting mutual attraction.
- Newer girl questioned whether I'd been seeing others, including whether anything had happened with my ex.
- Before meeting her, stayed polite when people flirted but generally gave them no encouragement.
- Liked her company and qualities; spent time as friends, taking much less initiative than usual.
- Ex claimed the newer girl couldn't compete because I retained feelings for the ex; some truth to that.
- Had mostly moved on from the ex by her return, but wasn't ready for the emotional disruption.
- Newer girl's willingness to accept my uncertainty was a major reason I felt drawn to her.
- She was hurt by the other encounters despite the agreed absence of exclusivity.
- Exclusivity felt imposed before I'd resolved my own difficulties; losing her earlier acceptance hurt.
- Attraction gradually faded after the change.
- Believe things were progressing naturally and could have satisfied both of us without the ex's interference.
- Offer personal experience relevant to someone describing a similar romantic arrangement.
- Show how outside interference and pressure to commit affected an initially promising connection.

(About me: Online relationship discussion participant. Length: it should come to roughly 400-800 words.)

must_cover: Describe how an initially undefined romantic arrangement developed while the writer still had unresolved feelings about an ex.
Describe the ex's interference and the subsequent decision to try monogamy.
Explain the eventual breakup and the writer's belief that pressure disrupted a promising connection.
Explain why the undefined arrangement initially suited them.
